sections.overview: Phalacrocorax fuscescens, the Black-faced Cormorant, is a cormorant endemic to southern Australia.
sections.identification: It is a medium-to-large black-and-white cormorant.
sections.habitat: It forages in coastal waters and sheltered bays.
sections.diet: It eats fish; one study found mostly benthic prey at a breeding site.
sections.behavior: It dives to forage and rests on offshore islets during trips.
sections.reproduction: It nests colonially on rocky islands and cliffs; breeding season varies regionally.
sections.ecology: This species is endemic to southern Australian coasts. P. varius also uses eastern inland wetlands.
sections.conservation: Population trends are uncertain; oil spills and marine debris pose risks.
